tasks.title: Implement read-only network inventory and Windows event sources
acceptance: Typed bounded event contracts
Connection inventory with clear collection scope
Event source health and permission failures are visible
No system-changing actions
Fixed-catalog EventLogWatcher subscriptions process future events through a bounded queue with visible loss/failure warnings
tasks.notes: Network inventory provides local interface counters/rates and up to 256 TCP endpoints. Event monitor samples 35 allow-listed v29 event IDs across 7 channels every 15 seconds; sources and alert projection have explicit partial/permission health. Services route provides bounded SCM enumeration (512 services, 16 pages), query-only startup-type lookup, separate output-only IPC, schema validation, and searchable WinUI list. No service management actions. Release build: 0 warnings/errors; full suite is now 59 passed. Remaining event parity: PowerShell Sigma/AMSI, richer detection, push subscriptions, Sysmon/ETW. See docs/WINDOWS_EVENTS.md.Active continuation: implement real-time EventLogWatcher subscriptions in addition to 15-second polling. Subscriptions must read only allow-listed metadata, keep a bounded queue and report loss/failure while preserving polling fallback. Test queue/batching/merge semantics without requiring enabled Windows event channels.Live collection now includes seven fixed-query EventLogWatcher subscriptions and a 512-record bounded nonblocking queue, coalesced into 256-row batches. Subscription failures and cumulative queue loss become source-health warnings; periodic 15-second polling remains fallback. 4625 push records are discarded so only the existing five-minute threshold aggregate is emitted. Release build clean; 74 tests pass. Local service smoke: 7/7 watcher subscriptions opened; poll could read 6/7 event channels. Real event delivery was not induced on the host. Source/docs pushed as e0720df plus release handoff docs; v0.1.8 published at https://github.com/christiand0797/downpour-next/releases/tag/v0.1.8. tasks.title: Package, sign, upgrade, recover, and release the Windows application
acceptance: Reproducible signed installer
Service lifecycle and least privilege documented
Upgrade, rollback, uninstall, and data recovery checked
tasks.notes: Portable updater shipped in v0.1.10 and v0.1.11, but user-reported laptop update ended in rollback. Root-cause review found the update helper was the running desktop executable and the containment check concatenated a second separator to a BaseDirectory path; the first caused an immediate failure, and replacing a running executable is not a valid Windows apply design. Current fix replaces this with a standalone single-file helper copied outside the install tree, canonical relative-path containment, visible detailed errors, and retry cleanup for safely validated failed staging. Source/build/tests are in progress for v0.1.12. Existing v0.1.10/v0.1.11 installs require a one-time manual overlay/extract of v0.1.12 because their embedded helper cannot self-replace safely. Then in-app updates use the standalone helper. Still required: end-to-end .11-to-.12 local apply, clean install update and rollback tests, independent signed update provenance, signed installer/rollback/uninstall.
